title: NCSC Cyber Drill — Demo
description: A minimal scored exercise used to validate the platform end to end.
outcomes: Reach a sandbox machine through the browser console
Locate a file on a remote host

levels.title: Welcome
levels.content:
# NCSC Cyber Drill — Demo

This short exercise checks that everything works: your environment, your access to it, and scoring.

| Level | Name | Type |
|:--:|---|---|
| 1. | Welcome | Info |
| 2. | Reach your environment | Access |
| 3. | Find the flag | Training |

You have your own private copy of this network. Nothing you do affects anyone else.

levels.title: Reach your environment
levels.cloud_content:
# Connect through the browser

Open the topology view, select the **client** machine, and choose **Open console in new window**.

If the topology view is blank, refresh the page.

Log in with:

- username: `participant`
- password: `ChangeMe123`

When you have a shell prompt, submit the passkey `connected` to continue.
levels.local_content:
# Connect over SSH

SSH access is available but is not used in this exercise. Use the browser console described in the other tab.

levels.title: Find the flag
levels.content:
# Find the flag

The **server** machine holds a file called `flag.txt`.

From your client machine, reach the server and read that file. Submit its contents as your answer.

The server is at `192.168.20.5`. Your client is at `192.168.30.5` — the two sit on different network segments, so your traffic crosses the routers between them.
levels.solution: From the client console: ssh participant@192.168.20.5 with the lab password, then run sudo cat /root/flag.txt. The hop crosses office-router and dmz-router.

hints.title: Where do I look?
hints.content: The flag is not on the client. It is on the **server** at 192.168.20.5 - a different network, reached through the routers.

hints.title: I can reach it but cannot read it
hints.content: The file is /root/flag.txt and only root can read it. The `participant` account exists on the server too and has sudo. Same password you used on the client.
